summary.suggested: The St. Louis Globe-Democrat, reprinting the Cincinnati Enquirer, reported that Joe Goss challenged Tom Allen to fight for $500 to $5,000 a side and the world championship, sending $500 to Eph Holland of Cincinnati.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Daily Globe-Democrat, Saturday Morning, April 29, 1876, page 5. Reprinted from the Cincinnati Enquirer.

facts.fact: Joe Goss, champion of England, challenged Allen from New York to fight in a 24-foot ring under London prize ring rules for $500 to $5,000 a side and the championship of the world, depositing $500 with Eph Holland, 101 West Fifth Street, Cincinnati
Allen had repeatedly said he would never deposit money with an Eastern stakeholder, claiming foul play by certain New York parties, and insisted on a Western stakeholder and a Western fight location
Allen had personal disputes with the New York Clipper and Wilkes' Spirit of the Times, which refused to print Goss's challenge to him

notes: Goss's letter says he would come to Cincinnati to make arrangements and train near there once Allen accepted.
